subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown abort active runs and their managed exec child processes, or preserve background/yielded exec sessions unless an explicit restart or kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, so changing this behavior is an operator-safety and product decision rather than a mechanical bug patch.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with an explicit documented exception for any background process class maintainers choose to preserve.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat this as a diagnostics/docs problem rather than a runtime cancellation change.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the process-control contract, then reuse that contract for gateway shutdown.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with an explicit documented exception for any background process class maintainers choose to preserve.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent process-supervisor and process-tool history, and the issue timeline already pulled him into this shutdown/process-control discussion.
